Looking for a free spinner that works for daily choices, team rituals, and event picks? These examples show how Wheelr can be your go-to wheel, prize wheel, wheel of fortune, and raffle tool for every online giveaway or group decision.

You can use it as a simple raffle picker, a free wheel for class games, or a live host flow to spin the wheel and build instant suspense. If your audience asks for spin for prizes free options or a fast raffle free setup, Wheelr gives you a clear and fun way to run every draw.

One evening, two friends spent 20 minutes arguing: "Should we order sushi, yes or no?" They used a yes or no wheel on this free spinner, spun once, got "Yes," and saved the night. It is the fastest way to stop overthinking and turn indecision into action.
Who does the house cleaning: fair and funny 🧹

In a shared apartment, "not me" became a daily tradition. They added all names to the wheel and let the wheel spinner pick who handles dishes, vacuum, and trash. No fights, no bias, just one transparent result from a playful wheel of fortune.
Who speaks first in a meeting: zero awkward silence 🎤

A remote team kept waiting for someone else to start. They built a speaking-order wheel and used it as a quick contest tool for standups. The spin broke the silence, everyone laughed, and meetings started on time.
Who wins the giveaway: live hype in seconds 🏆

During a livestream, the host needed a trusted wheel and raffle tool to pick a winner. With one spin, the audience saw a fair random result, chat exploded, and the online giveaway felt exciting, transparent, and professional. Perfect for any prize wheel moment.
Community raffle night: quick setup, trusted result 🎟️

A local group wanted a lightweight raffle flow without complicated forms. They entered participant names, clicked spin the wheel, and announced the winner in under a minute. It worked as a practical raffle free solution for small events and social clubs.

A small store launched a spin for prizes free corner to attract visitors. Customers used a branded free wheel at checkout, won discounts or gifts, and shared the moment on social media. The campaign felt fair, energetic, and easy to manage throughout the day.

How to use Wheelr step by step 🧭
This quick guide follows the same workflow shown in the official Wheelr article: from first setup to live extraction.
Open Wheelr and pick your mode. Start from the main page and decide whether you need one wheel or a multi-wheel layout (up to 4 wheels) for complex events.
Add participants or options. Insert names, prizes, or tasks in the entries list. Keep labels short so they stay readable during the spin.
Save presets from the wheel menu. Create different configurations (for example Junior Draw, Senior Draw, Gold Prizes) and switch instantly between them during the event.
Customize the visual identity. Set your segment colors, choose a custom background image, and configure the center area with a logo or text plus preferred size.
Choose your wheel font style. Select the font that best matches your brand or event tone so every wheel stays consistent and easy to read.
Set audio for suspense. Upload rotation, victory, and countdown sounds to make each extraction feel like a live show moment.
Configure the countdown timer. Enable countdown (for example 3, 2, 1) before the wheel spins to build anticipation in livestreams, classrooms, or office events.
Spin and announce the result. Click to spin, let the wheel stop naturally, then share the winner on screen for a transparent and fair draw.
Repeat quickly with presets or multiple wheels. For multi-phase sessions, load the next preset or switch wheel and continue without re-entering all names.
How do I make draws fairer?
Clean your names list, remove unwanted duplicates, and use Shuffle Names before every spin.
Can I use it in livestreams or classrooms?
Absolutely. Wheelr is perfect for public moments: everyone sees the result and engagement spikes instantly.
How can I make it more branded?
Customize colors, background, effects, and audio to match your team's identity or event tone.
Is it also good for light and funny decisions?
100%. From “who does the dishes” to “who picks the playlist,” the wheel settles debates in three seconds.

Add a Spin Wheel to Your Stream

A giveaway is worth watching when the audience sees the draw happen. Wheelr runs in a browser tab, hides its own interface on request, and can be captured by OBS or Streamlabs like any other window — no plugin, no account for your viewers, nothing to install.

1. Build the wheel first. Add your entries — viewer names, prizes, challenges — and set the colours, the centre logo and the sounds while the interface is still visible. Everything is saved on your device, so the wheel is still there for the next stream.
2. Hide the interface. The eye button in the side rail hides the header, the footer and every control, leaving the wheel alone on screen. Press it again to get the controls back.

3. Capture the window in OBS. Add a Window Capture source and point it at the browser window. Crop to the wheel and it behaves like any other scene element — resize it, move it, put it in a scene you switch to for the draw.

4. Spin on camera. Click the wheel in your browser window and the spin plays out live. The countdown before it starts and the winner effect afterwards are both there to give the moment room to breathe.
Floating the wheel over your scene

To put the wheel on top of your gameplay instead of on its own scene, give it a background your software can key out: open the colour settings, set the wheel background to a flat green such as #00FF00, then add a Color Key filter to the capture source in OBS. The wheel keeps its own colours and the green disappears.

Pick a green that appears nowhere on the wheel itself — if a slice is the same green, the filter will punch a hole through it. A colour palette without green, or a magenta key instead, avoids the problem entirely.

Sign in and save the wheel to the cloud, and it gets a public link you can drop in chat. Anyone who opens it sees the same entries in a read-only view — which is what makes a draw believable: the list was public before the spin, and it is still there afterwards.

Adding ?nobg=true to that public link strips the background and the page furniture, leaving just the wheel on a transparent page. It is a display, not a control: the shared view turns slowly on its own and cannot be spun, so use it as a panel or a second scene, and keep the spinning in your own window.

Every spin uses the browser's cryptographic random source, so nothing is seeded or weighted; slices of the same size have exactly the same chance. For a multi-prize giveaway, turn on removing the winner after each spin so nobody can win twice, and let the winners list build up on screen as the record of the session. Run several draws in parallel by showing up to four wheels side by side.
Does it work with Streamlabs, Twitch and YouTube?
Yes. Wheelr is a web page, so anything that can capture a browser window can put it on stream — OBS Studio, Streamlabs Desktop, XSplit. The platform you broadcast to makes no difference.
Do my viewers need an account?
No. A shared wheel opens in any browser with no signup. An account is only needed on your side, to publish the link and to reach your wheels from another device.
Can I match the wheel to my channel branding?
Colours, background, fonts, the centre logo and every sound are replaceable, so the wheel can carry your channel's look instead of a stock one. The setup is saved, so it is a one-off job.
How do I add hundreds of viewer names quickly?
Paste the whole list in one go rather than typing entries one by one, then shuffle before the first spin. On very long lists the labels get thin, so the winner is zoomed in on when the wheel stops.

Yes or No Wheel | Free Random Yes/No Spinner
Spin the yes or no wheel and get an answer in three seconds. A free random decision maker for the questions you keep going back and forth on. No signup.

Some questions do not deserve another twenty minutes of thinking. Spin the wheel, read the answer, move on. The result comes from your browser’s cryptographic random source, so it is genuinely unpredictable — nothing here is weighted or seeded.
When a wheel beats a coin flip

A coin gives you a private answer you can quietly ignore. A wheel spun in front of a group is a decision everyone watched happen, which is why it settles arguments that a coin does not. It is also slower on purpose: the three seconds of spinning are what make the answer feel earned rather than arbitrary.
Change the odds, or the answers

Copy the wheel and it becomes yours. Add more Yes slices than No ones if you already know which way you are leaning. Replace the two options entirely — "do it" and "not today", the names of two restaurants, two people who could take the task. The wheel does not care what is written on it.
Is the yes or no wheel really random?
Yes. The spin uses your browser’s cryptographic random number generator, the same source used for security keys. There is no seed, no pattern and no way to predict where it stops.
Can I add a third option like "maybe"?
Copy the wheel and add as many entries as you like. A third slice reading "ask again tomorrow" is a popular addition for questions that are not urgent.
Prize Wheel | Free Spin-to-Win Giveaway Picker
A free prize wheel for giveaways, live streams and events. Add your prizes, spin in front of your audience, and everyone sees the winner drawn fairly.

A giveaway is only as good as the moment the winner is announced. This prize wheel puts that moment on screen: the prizes are visible before the spin, the wheel slows down in front of everybody, and the result is impossible to quietly edit afterwards.

The wheel is designed to be shown, not just used: a countdown before the spin, a fireworks effect on the winner, and sounds you can swap for your own. Hide the interface chrome and the wheel fills the screen, which is what you want when it is sitting in a stream layout or on a projector at an event.

Put the prizes on the wheel and spin once per winner, or put the entrants on it and spin once per prize — both work. Winners can be removed automatically after each spin so nobody wins twice, and the winners list keeps the record of who drew what.
Every slice of the same size has exactly the same chance, and the outcome comes from a cryptographic random source rather than a seeded sequence. Nothing about the result can be set in advance.
Can my audience see the wheel without installing anything?
Yes. Publish the wheel as a read-only public link and anyone can open it in a browser, with no account. It is also what you share after the draw as a record of the entries.
What to Eat Wheel | Random Food Picker
Nobody can decide where to eat? Spin the food wheel and dinner is settled. A free random meal picker you can fill with your own restaurants and dishes.
"I don’t mind, you choose" is how a group loses half an hour. Put the options on a wheel, spin it once, and the question is closed — including for the person who said they did not mind.
Fill it with your actual options

The default wheel has the usual suspects, but it gets useful when you replace them with the eight places that actually deliver to you, or the meals you have ingredients for. Keep one wheel for weeknights and another for takeaway and switch between them — both stay saved on your device.

Spinning in front of everyone is the point: nobody has to be the one who decided, so nobody gets blamed for the choice. Add a "someone else picks" slice if you want an escape hatch, and remove options that got vetoed before you spin.
Can I save my own list of restaurants?
Yes. Copy the wheel, replace the entries with your own, and it stays on your device for next time. Signing in is optional and only needed to reach the same wheel from another device.
How many options can the food wheel hold?
Far more than a dinner decision needs. Past roughly a dozen the labels get tight, so a wheel of eight to ten options is the sweet spot for readability.
Random Team Generator | Free Group & Name Picker
Split a group into teams or pick a random person without the arguing. A free random team generator for classrooms, standups, workshops and game nights.

Picking teams by hand always ends with someone chosen last. A wheel removes the judgement from it: spin, read the name, move on to the next pick — and nobody can argue with a result nobody controlled.
Teams, turns and who goes first

The same wheel covers most group decisions: split a class into groups, choose who presents first in a standup, pick the volunteer nobody wants to be, or decide the order of a tournament. Remove each name as it comes up and the wheel works through the whole group without repeats.

Paste a list of names in one go rather than typing them one by one, shuffle before you start, and spin. In a classroom or a workshop the whole thing takes less time than reading the names out loud, and the visible spin is what keeps a room of people watching.
Can I stop the same person being picked twice?
Yes. Turn on removing the winner after each spin and every name is drawn at most once, so consecutive spins work through the group instead of repeating.
Can I run more than one team wheel at a time?
Up to four wheels can be shown side by side, each with its own entries — useful when you are drawing from separate pools, such as one wheel per team.
Truth or Dare Wheel | Free Party Game Spinner
A free truth or dare wheel for parties and game nights. Spin to decide, or fill it with your own truths and dares and let the wheel run the game.

The wheel does the part of truth or dare that nobody wants to do: choosing. Nobody picks on anybody, nobody goes easy on their friends, and the game keeps moving because there is nothing to negotiate.

Keep the wheel simple — truth or dare, spin per player — or write the actual challenges on the slices so the wheel hands out the dare itself. The second version is better for larger groups, where thinking of a new dare every turn is what slows the game down.
Set the tone before you spin

Copy the wheel and write your own entries, which is also how you keep the game appropriate for who is playing. A wheel written in advance by the whole group avoids the moment where one person invents a dare that goes too far.
Can I write my own truths and dares?
Yes — copy the wheel and replace the entries with anything you like. Your version is saved on your device, so the same wheel is ready for the next game night.
Does it work on a phone passed around the group?
It does. The wheel is designed for touch, fills the screen on a phone, and the interface can be hidden so only the wheel is visible while you play.
Discount Wheel | Free Spin-to-Win Promo Wheel
A free spin-to-win discount wheel for shops, market stalls and promos. Put your offers on the wheel and let customers spin for their own discount.

A discount someone won feels different from a discount they were given. Put your offers on the wheel, let the customer spin it themselves, and a routine promotion turns into thirty seconds of attention.
For a counter, a stall or a stand

Run it on a tablet at the till, on a laptop at a trade stand, or on a screen behind a market stall. Everything lives in the browser and the Android app works offline, which matters at an event where the venue wi-fi does not.
Control what you are giving away

The odds are the slices: make the deep discount one slice out of twelve and the small ones repeat. Adding a "next time" or "free shipping" slice keeps the wheel honest while capping what a single spin can cost you.
Can I control how often the big discount comes up?
Yes, through the slices themselves. Every slice of equal size has an equal chance, so repeating the smaller offers and leaving one slice for the big one sets the odds exactly.
Can I brand the wheel for my shop?
Colours, background, fonts, a centre logo and the sounds are all replaceable, so the wheel can be made to match your shop rather than looking like a generic tool.
What to Watch Wheel | Random Movie Picker
Stop scrolling and start watching. A free random movie picker: put the shortlist on the wheel, spin once, and the film is chosen for the night.
The half hour spent scrolling for something to watch is longer than the argument it was meant to avoid. Put the shortlist on a wheel, spin it, and the evening starts.

The wheel works best with the six or eight films everyone has already agreed they would accept. That is the real trick: the wheel is not choosing from everything, it is closing a list you have already narrowed down, which is the part a group cannot finish on its own.

Put genres on the wheel when nobody can even agree on a direction — spin once for the genre, then pick within it. The same wheel covers series nights, rewatches and the "something we have never seen" pile.
Can I keep a list of films for next time?
Yes. Copy the wheel, edit the entries, and it is saved on your device. You can keep several wheels — one for films, one for series, one for the list nobody has watched yet.
Can everyone watching see the wheel?
Share it as a read-only public link and anyone can open the same wheel in their browser with no account, which is handy when the group is not in the same room.
Random Workout Generator | Free Exercise Wheel
A free random workout generator: spin the wheel for your next exercise. Fill it with your own moves and let the wheel decide the order and the mix.

Training goes stale when you always pick the exercises you like. A wheel picks the ones you do not, keeps the session unpredictable, and removes the deciding from a moment when you would rather be resting.

Put the movements on the wheel and spin for the next one, or put durations and rep counts on a second wheel and spin both. Two wheels side by side — one for the exercise, one for the intensity — gives you a different session every time from the same list.
Build it around what you have

Write your own entries so the wheel only offers exercises you can actually do in the space and with the kit you own. A bodyweight wheel for travelling and a gym wheel for everything else is the usual split, and both stay saved.
Can I use it for HIIT or circuit training?
Yes. The countdown before each spin doubles as a rest timer, and removing each exercise after it comes up turns the wheel into a circuit that works through the whole list without repeats.
Does it work at the gym without a connection?
The Android app works fully offline, so a saved wheel keeps spinning in a basement gym with no signal.
Random Number Wheel | Free Number Picker Spinner
A free random number wheel: spin to draw a number in front of everyone. Set your own range for raffles, bingo, classroom picks and lotteries.
A number generator gives you a number. A wheel gives a room full of people a number they watched being drawn — which is what you need when the draw has to convince somebody other than you.

Raffle tickets, bingo calls, lottery-style draws, picking a seat or a locker: any time the number decides who gets something, being able to see it drawn matters more than the speed. The wheel slows the moment down deliberately, and the winners list keeps the order the numbers came out in.

Copy the wheel and replace the entries with whatever range you need — 1 to 20, ticket numbers, the numbers still in play. Remove each number after it is drawn and the wheel works through the range without repeating, which is exactly how a bingo caller uses it.
How is this different from a random number generator?

The randomness is the same cryptographic source. The difference is that the draw is visible: everyone watching sees the same spin land on the same number, which a generator that prints a number cannot offer.
Can I draw several numbers without repeats?
Yes. Turn on removing the winner after each spin and each number is drawn at most once, so repeated spins work through the whole range.
Icebreaker Questions Wheel | Free Team Spinner
A free icebreaker wheel for meetings, workshops and first days. Spin for a question, go round the room, and get a quiet group talking in two minutes.

Icebreakers fail when the facilitator picks the question and everyone can tell it was picked. A wheel takes that away: the question arrives by chance, the room reacts to the wheel instead of to you, and the first answer comes faster.

Spin once at the top of a recurring meeting and go round the room, or spin per person so everybody gets a different question. It works the same on a projector in a room and shared on a call, and two minutes is usually all it needs to take.
Write questions your team would answer

The stock questions are a starting point; the good version of this wheel is the one a team wrote themselves. Keep the questions light and answerable in a sentence — anything that needs a considered answer stops being an icebreaker and becomes a meeting.
Does it work for remote teams?
Yes. Share your screen and spin, or publish the wheel as a public link so everyone on the call opens the same one in their own browser.
Can I use my own icebreaker questions?
Copy the wheel and replace the entries with your own. The wheel is saved on your device, so the same set is ready for every following meeting.
Random Name Picker | Free Name Wheel Spinner
A free random name picker for classrooms, meetings and calls. Paste your list, spin the wheel, and the name is chosen in front of everyone.

Calling on someone is the moment a room decides whether you are fair. A wheel takes the choice out of your hands: the name is drawn in front of everybody, so nobody is picked on and nobody is skipped.

Add the whole list in one go rather than typing names one at a time, shuffle it, and start spinning. A teacher can set this up between two lessons, and the same wheel stays saved for the rest of the term.

Remove each name after it is drawn and the wheel works through the class without repeats — which is how you make sure the quiet students get their turn too. Leave the names in and it stays a lottery, better for handing out a single prize.
How many names can the picker hold?
A full class fits comfortably. Past roughly thirty entries the labels on the wheel get thin, so very long lists are easier to read split across a few wheels.
Can I stop a name from being picked twice?
Yes. Turn on removing the winner after each spin and each name is drawn at most once, so consecutive spins work through the whole list.
Would You Rather Wheel | Free Question Spinner
A free would you rather wheel: spin for an impossible choice and make everyone defend their answer. Add your own questions in seconds.
The hard part of would you rather is thinking of a question that nobody has heard before. Let the wheel hold the questions, and the game runs itself — spin, read it out, go round the group.
Good for a queue, a car or a classroom

It needs no setup and no props, which is why it works in the places where a game normally cannot start: waiting somewhere, a long drive, the last ten minutes of a lesson. One phone passed around is enough.
Write the questions for your group

Copy the wheel and replace the entries with dilemmas aimed at the people playing — in-jokes, work scenarios, questions only your friends would find funny. A wheel written by the group is always better than a generic list.
Can I add my own would you rather questions?
Yes. Copy the wheel, replace the entries with your own, and your version is saved on your device for the next time you play.
How do I keep it suitable for kids?
Write the wheel in advance with the questions you are happy with. Because the wheel only ever offers what is written on it, there are no surprises mid-game.
Never Have I Ever Wheel | Free Party Game Spinner
A free never have I ever wheel for game nights. Spin for the prompt, see who owns up, and add your own statements whenever you like.
Never have I ever stalls the moment somebody has to invent the next statement. Put them on a wheel and the game keeps its rhythm: spin, read it out, watch who gives themselves away.

Nobody has to run the game, which also means nobody can aim a statement at one person in particular. The wheel picking at random is what keeps it light — everyone is exposed by chance rather than by the person whose turn it was.

The default statements are mild on purpose. Copy the wheel and write your own for the group you are playing with, and keep more than one version — a work-party wheel and a close-friends wheel are not the same list.
How many players does it work with?
Any number. The wheel only picks the statement; how you score it — fingers down, points, forfeits — is up to the group.
Can everyone see the wheel at once?
Share it as a read-only public link and everyone opens the same wheel in their own browser, or put one screen in the middle of the table.
Chore Wheel | Free Chore Chart Spinner
A free chore wheel for housemates and families. Spin to assign the washing up, the bins and everything nobody volunteers for — without the argument.
Every shared house has the same argument, and it is never really about the dishes. A wheel settles it without anyone having to be the one who decided: spin, read the result, it is done.
Chores or people — pick a side

Put the chores on the wheel and spin once per person, or put the housemates on it and spin once per chore. The second version is better when one job is far worse than the others, because everybody watches that particular spin.

Add a "day off" slice so there is something to hope for, and remove each chore once it is assigned so the wheel shares out the whole list. Keep the wheel saved and re-spin it every Sunday — the routine is what stops the argument coming back.
Can I add or remove chores?
Yes. Copy the wheel and edit the entries to match your household — the version you make is saved on your device.
Can I make one chore rarer than the others?
The odds are just the slices. Repeat the chores you want to come up more often and leave the worst one as a single slice.
Secret Santa Wheel | Free Gift Exchange Name Draw
Draw Secret Santa names with a wheel instead of a hat. Free, works for an office or a family, and everyone sees the draw happen.
A hat full of folded paper only works when everyone is in the same room. A wheel draws the names in front of whoever is watching — in the office, on a call, or in a group chat with the screen shared.
